title: Exploratory species guesses for unidentified turtle sightings
description: Low-confidence geographic-prior guesses for the four 2006 survey observations. They are not species identifications, validated model outputs, or migration tracks. The original observation records remain unidentified.

method.name: regional range prior
method.summary: The sightings are from the Northwest Atlantic near 40 degrees north in late July. Loggerheads are a plausible regional species, so loggerhead is selected as a single heuristic best guess for each observation.
limitations: The observations were recorded only as unidentified turtle (Chelonioidea).
All four points are from one survey, close in place and time, and have no species-diagnostic fields.
The documented regional range does not establish the identity of an individual sighting.
Other sea turtle species may occur in the broader Northwest Atlantic.
No training data, calibrated probabilities, or independent validation were used.
Do not use these labels as confirmed species data, species-specific migration routes, or scientific estimates.

predictions.rationale: Plausible regional species based on Northwest Atlantic range; the observation itself has no species-identifying evidence.
